library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Baek_2014_cyclosporine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Baek_2014_cyclosporine"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S70595>

Baek 2014 followed oral micro-emulsified cyclosporine (CsA) through the
non-steady-state first week after living-donor renal transplantation. Full
12-hour profiles on postoperative days (POD) 2, 3 and 7 were fitted with a
two-compartment model with first-order absorption and a lag time. Disposition
was held constant across the week. The absorption parameters (ka, lag time
and relative bioavailability F1) were allowed to change between study days,
and they did: ka rose 4.56-fold from POD 2 to POD 3, the lag time 1.15-fold,
and F1 rose 1.09-fold and then fell again by POD 7.

# Population

Sixty-nine adult Korean recipients of a first living-donor kidney (Samsung
Medical Center, Seoul) were enrolled: mean age 41.2 years (SD 10.6, range
16-63), mean body weight 58.7 kg (SD 10.2, range 38.9-97.6), 31 women and 38
men (Table 1). All received CsA, mycophenolate mofetil 1,500 mg/day and
tapering methylprednisolone without induction therapy. CsA was given as 4
mg/kg IV on POD 1 and then as 8 mg/kg/day oral micro-emulsion (Cipol-N soft
capsule) in two divided doses from POD 2, titrated to a trough of 300-350
ng/mL. Whole blood was sampled pre-dose and at 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 h after
the morning dose on POD 2, 3 and 7; two patients with acute rejection missed
the POD 7 profile, leaving 1,640 concentrations. Genotype frequencies (ABCB1
3435C>T, CYP3A4, CYP3A5) are in Table 2; none was retained as a covariate.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Baek_2014_cyclosporine")()$population`.

# Virtual cohort

Two hundred virtual recipients are drawn with weight and age from normal
distributions matching the Table 1 mean and SD, truncated to the observed
ranges.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2014)
n_sub <- 200
rtnorm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  while (any(out <- x < lo | x > hi)) x[out] <- rnorm(sum(out), mean, sd)
  x
}
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = rtnorm(n_sub, 58.7, 10.2, 38.9, 97.6),
  AGE = rtnorm(n_sub, 41.2, 10.6, 16, 63)
)
summary(cohort[, c("WT", "AGE")])
```

# Dosing and simulation

Time zero is the first oral dose, the morning of POD 2. Each recipient takes
4 mg/kg every 12 hours (the starting 8 mg/kg/day regimen) through the morning
dose of POD 7, and is sampled at the study times after the morning dose of POD
2, 3 and 7. `POD` is supplied on every row as `2 + floor(time / 24)`.

```{r events}
dose_times <- seq(0, 120, by = 12)
pk_days <- c(2, 3, 7)
nominal <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12)
obs_times <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(pk_days, function(d) {
  (d - 2) * 24 + c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), nominal)
}))))

doses <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = dose_times) |>
  mutate(amt = 4 * WT, evid = 1, cmt = "depot")
obs <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  mutate(POD = 2 + floor(time / 24)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

mod <- readModelDb("Baek_2014_cyclosporine")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2014)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(
    POD = 2 + floor(time / 24),
    tad = time - (POD - 2) * 24
  ) |>
  filter(POD %in% pk_days, tad <= 12) |>
  mutate(pod_label = factor(paste("POD", POD), levels = paste("POD", pk_days)))
```

# Replicate Figure 3 (VPC by study day)

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Baek 2014: median (solid) and 90% prediction interval (dashed) of whole-blood cyclosporine after the morning dose on POD 2, 3 and 7."}
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(tad %in% nominal) |>
  group_by(pod_label, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# The POD 2 pre-dose sample is zero (no IV dose) and cannot go on a log axis.
ggplot(filter(vpc, p50 > 0), aes(tad)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~pod_label) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(50, 3000)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = nominal) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Cyclosporine (ng/mL)")
```

The published Figure 3 draws the same prediction lines in all three panels
(median about 870 ng/mL at 2 h and about 200 ng/mL at 12 h) and overlays each
day's observations, so the per-day comparison is against the observed points.
The values below were read by eye from Figure 3 by the maintainers and are
approximate.

* **POD 3.** The observed points at 6, 8 and 12 h centre near 450, 300 and
  200 ng/mL, matching the simulated medians (`r round(vpc$p50[vpc$pod_label == "POD 3" & vpc$tad == 6])`,
  `r round(vpc$p50[vpc$pod_label == "POD 3" & vpc$tad == 8])` and
  `r round(vpc$p50[vpc$pod_label == "POD 3" & vpc$tad == 12])` ng/mL). The
  observed 2-h values centre near 1,000 ng/mL, below the simulated
  `r round(vpc$p50[vpc$pod_label == "POD 3" & vpc$tad == 2])` ng/mL, so the
  simulated POD 3 peak is somewhat sharper than the data.
* **POD 7.** The observed points sit about 20-30% below the simulated medians
  at every time, troughs included (observed about 160-170 ng/mL against a
  simulated `r round(vpc$p50[vpc$pod_label == "POD 7" & vpc$tad == 12])`
  ng/mL at 12 h). A uniform offset of this kind is what a lower average dose
  gives, and the study doses were titrated to the trough rather than held at 4
  mg/kg.
* **POD 2.** The simulation starts at the first oral dose and leaves out the
  POD 1 intravenous dose, so the simulated pre-dose concentration is zero
  where the observed values centre near 170 ng/mL. The simulated late
  concentrations are correspondingly lower than the observations, and the
  slower POD 2 absorption shows as a lower 1-h median than on POD 3 or POD 7.

The individual doses in the study are not reported, so absolute levels are
not expected to match exactly.

# Typical-value checks against the closed form

A typical 60 kg, 41.2-year-old recipient is given a single 240 mg oral dose
with `POD` held at 2, 3 or 7, with random effects removed. For a linear
model, AUC0-inf is `F1 * Dose / (k * V2)`, so the ratios of AUC0-inf between
days must equal the bioavailability ratios in Table 3: 1.09 from POD 2 to POD
3, and 0.807 from POD 3 to POD 7 at the reference age.

```{r typical}
typ_grid <- c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.1), seq(24.5, 400, by = 0.5))
typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(c(2, 3, 7), function(p) {
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = p, time = 0, amt = 240, evid = 1, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = p, time = typ_grid, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(POD = p, WT = 60, AGE = 41.2)
}))
# Three typical subjects (one per POD) with omega removed: rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the intent here.
typ <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega"),
    events = typ_events, returnType = "data.frame",
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
  ),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
) |>
  mutate(POD = id)

typ_conc <- typ |> select(POD, time, Cc)
typ_dose <- typ_events |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(POD, time, amt)
typ_nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(typ_conc, Cc ~ time | POD),
  PKNCAdose(typ_dose, amt ~ time | POD),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)
))
typ_res <- as.data.frame(typ_nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  select(POD, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  select(POD, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs)

# Closed form, ng*h/mL: F1 * Dose / (k * V2) * 1000
f_rel <- c(`2` = 1, `3` = 1.09, `7` = 1.09 * 0.807)
typ_res$auc_closed <- f_rel[as.character(typ_res$POD)] * 240 / (0.254 * 142) * 1000

typ_res |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf.obs / auc_closed - 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "POD" = POD,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf, simulated (ng*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs,
    "AUC0-inf, closed form (ng*h/mL)" = auc_closed,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

auc <- setNames(typ_res$aucinf.obs, typ_res$POD)
stopifnot(
  # The solve and the closed form share every parameter, so the only
  # difference is trapezoidal and extrapolation error (measured < 0.1%).
  all(abs(typ_res$aucinf.obs / typ_res$auc_closed - 1) < 0.01),
  abs(auc[["3"]] / auc[["2"]] / 1.09 - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(auc[["7"]] / auc[["3"]] / 0.807 - 1) < 0.005
)
```

The POD 3 increase in ka moves the typical Tmax earlier and raises Cmax
beyond what the 9% gain in bioavailability alone would give.

## Age dependence of the POD 7 bioavailability change (Figure 2C)

```{r fig2c, fig.cap = "Typical D7F1 = 0.807 * (age / 41.2)^-0.293 over the observed age range; compare the individual estimates and smooth in Figure 2C of Baek 2014."}
age_curve <- tibble(AGE = seq(16, 63, by = 1)) |>
  mutate(d7f1 = 0.807 * (AGE / 41.2)^-0.293)
ggplot(age_curve, aes(AGE, d7f1)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "D7F1 (POD 7 vs POD 3 relative bioavailability)")
```

The typical value falls from 1.06 at 16 years to 0.71 at 63 years. The
published smooth through the individual estimates runs from about 0.93 to
about 0.69 over the same range. That smooth runs through individual
(empirical Bayes) estimates, which shrink toward the population value, rather
than tracing the typical-value curve.

## Individual parameters in the stochastic cohort

The medians of the individual absorption changes across the virtual cohort
should sit at the Table 3 typical values, because each change is log-normal
around its typical value.

```{r indiv}
ind <- sim |>
  filter(tad == 0) |>
  select(id, POD, ka, tlag, fdepot) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = POD, values_from = c(ka, tlag, fdepot))
chk <- tibble(
  quantity = c(
    "ka POD 3 / POD 2", "ka POD 7 / POD 3", "lag POD 3 / POD 2",
    "F1 POD 3 / POD 2"
  ),
  table3 = c(4.56, 1, 1.15, 1.09),
  simulated_median = c(
    median(ind$ka_3 / ind$ka_2), median(ind$ka_7 / ind$ka_3),
    median(ind$tlag_3 / ind$tlag_2), median(ind$fdepot_3 / ind$fdepot_2)
  )
)
chk |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Table 3 typical value" = table3,
    "Simulated median" = simulated_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # The lag-time change has no BSV, so it is exact.
  abs(chk$simulated_median[3] / 1.15 - 1) < 1e-6,
  # F1 ratio: log-SD 0.127, so the SE of the median of 200 is about 1.1%.
  abs(log(chk$simulated_median[4] / 1.09)) < 0.05,
  # ka ratio: log-SD 1.18 (174% CV), SE of the median of 200 about 0.10 on
  # the log scale; 0.4 is roughly 4 SE and still fails on a misplaced eta.
  abs(log(chk$simulated_median[1] / 4.56)) < 0.4
)
```

# NCA of the simulated profiles

PKNCA is run on each 12-hour profile after the morning dose, grouped by study
day.

```{r nca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, pod_label, tad, Cc)
dose_df <- conc_df |>
  distinct(id, pod_label) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  mutate(tad = 0, amt = 4 * WT)

nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ tad | pod_label + id),
  PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ tad | pod_label + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = 12,
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
  )
))
nca_sum <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  group_by(pod_label, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE),
    p05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(summary = sprintf("%.3g (%.3g-%.3g)", median, p05, p95)) |>
  select(pod_label, PPTESTCD, summary) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = summary)
nca_sum |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Study day" = pod_label,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin,
    "AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median (5th-95th percentile) of simulated NCA parameters at 4 mg/kg every 12 h.")
```

Cmin on POD 2 is zero because the simulated pre-dose sample precedes the
first oral dose. The paper reports no NCA summary, so there is no published
table to compare against; the profiles above are checked against the Figure 3
observations instead.

# Single concentrations as predictors of AUC0-12 (Table 4)

Table 4 of the paper correlates each sampled concentration with the
linear-trapezoid AUC0-12 on each study day. The same calculation on the
simulated nominal samples:

```{r table4}
nom <- sim |>
  filter(tad %in% nominal) |>
  select(id, pod_label, tad, sim) |>
  group_by(id, pod_label) |>
  arrange(tad, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(auc012 = sum(diff(tad) * (head(sim, -1) + tail(sim, -1)) / 2)) |>
  ungroup()
r_sim <- nom |>
  # The simulated POD 2 pre-dose sample is zero for everyone (no IV dose).
  filter(!(pod_label == "POD 2" & tad == 0)) |>
  group_by(pod_label, tad) |>
  summarise(r = cor(sim, auc012), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(source = "Simulated")
r_pub <- tibble(
  pod_label = factor(rep(paste("POD", pk_days), each = 8), levels = paste("POD", pk_days)),
  tad = rep(nominal, 3),
  r = c(
    0.5215, 0.2418, 0.3323, 0.4346, 0.4925, 0.6868, 0.7013, 0.6834,
    0.4849, 0.4397, 0.5886, 0.5908, 0.6712, 0.6568, 0.7199, 0.5457,
    0.5291, 0.5710, 0.7536, 0.7544, 0.6841, 0.6082, 0.6489, 0.6823
  ),
  source = "Baek 2014 Table 4 (overall)"
)
bind_rows(r_sim, r_pub) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, r, colour = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~pod_label) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = nominal) +
  labs(x = "Sampling time after dose (h)", y = "Correlation with AUC0-12", colour = NULL)
```

```{r table4-best}
best <- function(d) {
  d |>
    group_by(pod_label) |>
    slice_max(r, n = 1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    transmute(pod_label, best = sprintf("C%g (r = %.2f)", tad, r))
}
best(r_sim) |>
  rename(simulated = best) |>
  left_join(best(r_pub) |> rename(published = best), by = "pod_label") |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Study day" = pod_label,
    "Best single time, simulated" = simulated,
    "Best single time, Table 4" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

On POD 7 the simulation agrees with Table 4: the 2-3 h samples track AUC0-12
best, which is the paper's case that early sampling only becomes informative
once absorption has recovered. On POD 3 the simulated best time (6 h) is close
to the published 8 h, with the 4-8 h samples nearly tied in both. POD 2 does
not agree: in the simulation the 3-h sample correlates best and the late
samples worst, whereas in the paper the 6-12 h samples correlate best. The
simulation leaves out the POD 1 intravenous dose, whose carry-over makes up a
large share of the late POD 2 concentrations, and it does not reproduce the
individually titrated doses. The comparison is therefore qualitative, and it
is not informative on POD 2.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Between-subject variability scale.** Table 3 reports BSV as CV% without a
  definition. The exact log-normal conversion `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` is
  used. If the authors meant `CV = 100 * sqrt(omega^2)`, the variances of the
  three ka terms (136%, 174%, 268%) would be larger (1.85, 3.03 and 7.18
  instead of 1.05, 1.39 and 2.10); the bootstrap percentile intervals in
  Table 3 cannot discriminate between the two readings, and simulating
  both shows that the median profiles barely differ (the POD 3 2-h median
  moves by about 4%), so Figure 3 cannot settle it either.
* **Lag time on POD 7.** Table 3 defines the lag time only on POD 2 (INLA)
  and POD 3 (INLA * D3LA) and lists no POD 7 term. POD 7 is given the POD 3
  value, following the cumulative pattern Table 3 uses for ka and F1, where
  each later day multiplies the previous day's value.
* **POD between and beyond the study days.** The model is defined for POD 2,
  3 and 7. POD 4-6 take the POD 3 values and POD after 7 the POD 7 values;
  neither was sampled.
* **Relative bioavailability.** F1 is relative to POD 2, so V2, V3, Q and
  CL = k * V2 are apparent values scaled by the unknown absolute oral
  bioavailability on POD 2. The model is for oral dosing only; the POD 1
  intravenous dose cannot be represented on the same scale and is omitted
  from the simulations.
* **BSV fixed to zero.** BSV on k, on the lag time and on D3LA was not
  estimable (Table 3) and is omitted rather than encoded as a zero variance.
  D7KA is fixed to 1 but kept to carry its BSV, as in the source.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** Sex, CYP3A5 genotype and ABCB1
  (MDR1) 3435C>T genotype were tested and not retained. ABCB1 carriers had a
  larger individual POD 7 change in ka (post hoc P = 0.002), but the genotype
  was left out because it inflated the standard errors. These are documented
  under `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Dosing in the simulations.** The virtual recipients stay on 4 mg/kg every
  12 h; the study titrated the dose to a 300-350 ng/mL trough, and the actual
  doses are not reported.
* **Erratum check.** No erratum or correction was found in Europe PMC (searched
  2026-11-23).
